title: Simplify to vector when parsing json message for R
description:
So that we get vector instead of unnamed list as e.g some knitr options expect vector. This closes #3909

## Context 

Setting multiple for `dev` was not working 
````markdown
---
title: "Document"
format: 
  html:
    embed-resources: false
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    dev:
      - png
      - pdf
      - svg
---

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot() + ggtitle("this is a title")
```
````

because Quarto parses the YAML then pass it to the R process using JSON message that is parsed with **jsonlite** but `knitr$opts_chunk$dev` is seen as a unamed list and not coerced to a vector. 

This creates issue within **knitr** which expect a vector for some options and currently does not handle or coerce list to vector itself. 

I believe that YAML parsing does correctly see this as a vector, so it seems ok to simplify when parsing the JSON. 
This will also convert to Matrix and Dataframe in some case - if we want to prevent that we could do 
````
request <- jsonlite::parse_json(input, simplifyVector = TRUE, simplifyDataFrame = FALSE, simplifyMatrix = FALSE)
````
but seems too much. 

If this is too broad fix anyway, We could simplify only the `knitr` fields in the message.;

BTW I tried to add a test using the new smoke-all folder - Hopefully adding a file is enough for it to be run.

title: Feature/code annote
description:
Basic code annotation (supported generally with some special sauce mixed in to HTML). Write a document like so:

````markdown
---
title: Test Code Annotation
author: Norah Jones
date: last-modified
format: html
---

## Where You At

```{r}
#| label: fig-plot
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: Bro this chart is fire and is definitely not sus.
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw())  


data("mtcars") # <1>
mtcars$`car name` <- rownames(mtcars)  # <2>
mtcars$mpg_z <- round((mtcars$mpg - mean(mtcars$mpg))/sd(mtcars$mpg), 2)  # <3>
mtcars$mpg_type <- ifelse(mtcars$mpg_z < 0, "below", "above")  # <4>
mtcars <- mtcars[order(mtcars$mpg_z), ]  # <5>
mtcars$`car name` <- factor(mtcars$`car name`, levels = mtcars$`car name`)  # <6>

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=`car name`, y=mpg_z, label=mpg_z)) + # <7> 
  geom_bar(stat='identity', aes(fill=mpg_type), width=.5)  + # <7> 
  scale_fill_manual(name="Mileage", # <7> 
                    labels = c("Above Average", "Below Average"), # <7> 
                    values = c("above"="#00ba38", "below"="#f8766d")) + 
  labs(subtitle="Normalised mileage from 'mtcars'", # <7> 
       title= "Diverging Bars") + # <7> 
  coord_flip() # <8> 
```

1. `mtcars` is a built in data set that we'll use for the purposes of making this plot. For more about built in data sets in R, see <https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/Rdatasets/>
2. Here, we're creating a new column for car names (for display purposes).
3. Normalize the computed miles per gallon
4. Flag mileage as above or below average. This will make it easier to use a color to represent whether the mileage is above or below average.
5. Sort the data by mileage.
6. Convert this to a factor in order to retain the sorted order when used in a plot. I don't know what this means, but its all good.
7. Actually render the diverging bar chart, which will result in a really awesome chart that you can't even believe.

````

title: new download implementation - prep for platform refactor
description:
# TODO:

* [x] refactor existing places using download to downloadFile

# summary

This PR implements a new download functionality with a bit more error handling and control built in. In addition it sets up vscode launch files to run tests.

The design mirrors the go-idiom of using interfaces were possible, thus the base `download` function has been adjusted from a string dest to a writer. This makes it a little more unwieldy to use quickly, but gives a lot of flexibility, including things like being able to just pull down into a buffer to manipulate rather than even needing to write out to the file system. 

In addition, I added a response validator so can do some introspection of the response. The particular case in mind is valid URLs that aren't actual files might end up dumping nonsense data. I've had this issue before writing tooling that downloaded packages from cranlike repos and the naive implementation would still dump just like an HTML page that said "not authorized" or whatever since it was still a successful response. 

As such, it makes sense to consider this something fine to use, but nice to build abstraction(s) on. To keep it consistent as possible with the existing download implementation, I've added a higher level `downloadFile` which still maintains the same interface (well extended the src to also take a URL), but the string filepath. This also is gated to confirm against one of the known content-types for files that we need to download.

This will fix one existing error - currently on the existing download when downloading the esbuild tarballs, it does the exact issue above (with no reponse validator) on arm platforms, dumping out a text file, and then it is the untar function that explodes when it identifies its not operating on an archive.

PS. random aside - the deno manual was out of date for testing on 1.17 which was quite the head scratcher trying to write some tests and trying to figure out why assertThrowsAsync didn't exist according to the compiler, so I ended up adding a tiny patch there to update that - https://github.com/denoland/manual/pull/196 so if you're reading through the manual for now for testing, look at the `main` branch instead of 1.17 for the moment 🤪 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3196313/148239554-c6f732f5-c29b-4f3b-9da9-e513377f4a07.png)

title: use plain table for theorem types
description:
Bug originally reported by @andrie

MRE is any div with a three letter prefix that doesn't match one of the theorem or proof types, e.g.

```markdown
::: {#new-platforms}
:::
```

Will result in this error:

```bash
Error running filter C:/Users/apdev/AppData/Local/Programs/Quarto/share/filters/crossref/crossref.lua:
...ocal/Programs/Quarto/share/filters/crossref/crossref.lua:2096: attempt to index a function value (local 'theoremType')
stack traceback:
	...ocal/Programs/Quarto/share/filters/crossref/crossref.lua:1239: in function <...ocal/Programs/Quarto/share/filters/crossref/crossref.lua:1233>
```

Error traced to the fact that our lookup table for theorem types uses `pandoc.List`, which returns a function for a missed key lookup with brackets (in this case `theoremTypes["new"]`) which passes our `nil` check.

This change turns it into an ordinary Lua table, which matches the semantics of all of its uses (it is basically indexed using `[]` and `tkeys()` is called on it.

title: Add `connection` among known knitr opts
description:
This closes #2310 

`connection` was not among the known **knitr** option which which was leading to a JSON conversion not possible.
https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/e1cddd0d424aba2fcf8d2d1af0a7a7e7fc36c69d/src/resources/rmd/hooks.R#L277-L285

This PR adds `connection` as a know option so that current **knitr** syntax does not throw an error and works 

````markdown
```{sql, connection = con}
SELECT manufacturer, displ, cty
FROM mpg
ORDER BY manufacturer, displ DESC
```
````

Other Quarto recommended syntax does works 
```{sql}
#| connection: con
SELECT manufacturer, displ, cty
FROM mpg
ORDER BY manufacturer, displ DESC
```

because **knitr** supports `connection` to be a string.  However, IDE does not support this interactively yet (https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/11606)

This is why the first syntax is important for RStudio user with Quarto also. 


I took the opportunity to add test for SQL chunks. This was necessary to add DBI and RSQLite in **renv**. 

So I also took the liberty to update **renv** environment, so that we run test on latest version of packages. 

Opening this as Draft to check that smoke tests still run fine with this change.

title: [revealjs] pin to commit hash version to get fix on slide scaling
description:
Current version use `zoom` attributes which messes up JS lib like plotly. This new version using `scale()` transform only.

This fixes #2430

Steps were
* Set commit hash in configuration file
* Adapt `update-html-dependencies` for reveal to use commit instead of tags
* Run `quarto-bld.cmd update-html-dependencies` 
* Only kept RevealJS update in the PR (as other deps were also updated). 

Tested using version built with  `./configure.cmd` using example in the issue. The tooltip issue disappeared. 

I made a PR so that it is easier to test, I don't know if we want to update to a commit, or wait for a next release of Revealjs. 

Feel free to dismiss if it is not desired now.

title: Ignore windows env configuration file
description:
This file is created by `package\src\store_win_configuration.bat` during `configure.cmd`

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/6a5916830c24e6e3f93454f78b6c0dc717f8e42f/package/src/store_win_configuration.bat#L19-L22

Currently this file is stored in Git. When running `configure.cmd`, it gets modified and is unsynced with current version commited in the repo. This is because last update did only update the linux configuration file which it is based of. 

As this file is generated automatically based on `configuration` I don't think we need to have it in git. 

Otherwise, we need to commit the modification each time so that we keep a clean sync state of the repo. 

Current diff of this file when running `configure.cmd` from main branch which shows it is out of date
````diff
diff --git a/win_configuration.bat b/win_configuration.bat                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
index ef28685f8..b1cd5e997 100644
--- a/win_configuration.bat
+++ b/win_configuration.bat
@@ -1,10 +1,10 @@
 REM This file is generated by the package/src/store_win_configuration.bat script.
 REM   Do not edit it manually.
-SET "DENO=v1.22.0"
-SET "DENO_DOM=v0.1.17-alpha"
+SET "DENO=v1.25.1" 
+SET "DENO_DOM=v0.1.23-alpha-artifacts" 
 SET "PANDOC=2.19.2"
 SET "DARTSASS=1.32.8"
-SET "ESBUILD=0.14.39"
+SET "ESBUILD=0.15.6" 
 SET "BOOTSTRAP=888fbe064491692deb56fd90dc23455052e31073"
 SET "BOOTSTRAP_FONT=1.8.1"
 SET "BOOTSWATCH=5.1.3"
@@ -24,9 +24,9 @@ SET "AUTOCOMPLETE_JS=1.5.3"
 SET "FUSE_JS=6.5.3"
 SET "ALGOLIA_SEARCH_JS=4.5.1"
 SET "ALGOLIA_SEARCH_INSIGHTS_JS=2.0.3"
-SET "QUARTO_VERSION=1.1"
+SET "QUARTO_VERSION=1.2" 
 SET "QUARTO_NAME=Quarto"
-SET "QUARTO_BUILD_RUN_OFFSET=-1289"
+SET "QUARTO_BUILD_RUN_OFFSET=-1420"
````

title: Configure the Github Issue chooser
description:
To add some more choices when a user go to the issue workflow

Doc about this Github feature in https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/configuring-issue-templates-for-your-repository#configuring-the-template-chooser

The proposal is to have something like in **rmarkdown** (https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/new/choose) 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6791940/188452036-58cf1315-e8ac-45fd-9071-819f0a44ee9d.png)

or in RStudio IDE (https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/new/choose)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6791940/188452170-c458ae51-4f03-4ea1-9bad-75753ebe4773.png)

Proposal: 

* Issues are opened in the repo following the template
* Link to issue guide is shared from the chooser so that user know where to find it even before opening an issue
* Questions should be opened to https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/categories/q-a so we share a link to the category directly
* Any type of feedback can be shared in our Dicussion board, and the last link point to Discussion. 

The two last could be merged in one link.

`blank_issues_enabled: false` means it is not possible to open a blank issue - I think it is valid as we allow discussion board for anything so that if someone does not want to open a Bug, then it will be a new discussion (we could convert to issue). 

This is a first proposal to have a more welcoming page when someone click on "New Issue" in this repo.

support raw html tables in all formats
description:
If we have a raw html table in a format that doesn't handle raw_html then have pandoc parse the table into a proper AST table block.

The motivation for this is to resolve this issue: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/724. 

ipynb files are not executed by default when rendered (as the output is already embedded and it may not even be possible to re-execute given the rendering environment, availability of dependencies, etc.). This means that we need to rely on the representation created in the interactive notebook. For tables, this will often be HTML. Without attempting to interpret the HTML, this makes ipynb files with tables un-renderable to non-HTML formats (e.g. pdf, docx, ec.)

This PR has two main changes:

1) When marshaling from` ipynb` to `md` prior to rendering, include raw HTML output if it includes a `<table>` tag.

2) For formats that can't render HTML tables natively (e.g. pdf, docx, rtf, odt, etc.), read raw HTML tables into the pandoc AST (which allows them to be rendered in their native format)

title: Add `uses` support to SCSS theme file format
description: This allows Quarto theme themes to include `@use` statements which will be relocated to the front of the merged scss file. In addition, this PR adds the directory containing any user theme that is being applied to the load path for the scss compiler, allowing easier discovery of imports and uses... Note that in many cases, `@import` will be preferable (despite the global scope) because `@use` statements _must_ appear before defaults, functions, mixins, and rules, so they cannot depend upon defaults, for example. `import` statements can be placed inline making them able to appear with rules, for example, to take advantage of variables that have been defined... #### Theme #### File location (note `theme.scss` and `a11y-color.scss` in same dir #### Use Syntax (Note that `a11y-color` won't really work in `use` without modification because it depends upon `$white` and `$black` being defined). #### Import Example (This actually works and shows that since the `theme.scss` directory is added to load paths, we're able to import the scss file).

title: Improve the creation of citations
description:
Bug #1609 has a number of great suggestions for improving citation metadata for documents. This addresses most of those suggestions, generating additional `citation_` meta tags based upon document citation data as well as making our handling of citation data more consistent.

We will newly output:
`citation_abstract`
`citation_doi`
`citation_pmid`
`citation_language`
`citation_keywords`
`citation_pdf_url`
`citation_public_url`
`citation_abstract_url`
`citation_fulltext_url`
`citation_journal_abbrev`
`citation_publisher`

Based upon the `type` specified:
`citation_conference_title`/`citation_conference`
`citation_dissertation_institution`
`citation_book_title`

General approach is to allow specification of citation data with names and structure that corresponds with CSL schema and to map those values onto the appropriate meta names (rather than matching the meta names directly).

description:
This will be to remove when pandoc's template changes. This also removed a previous patched not needed anymore

For context and documentation,  this is something that happened following a Pandoc change in template, and we never dealt with the change. See our dicussion https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/pull/147#discussion_r735591791

The initial fix was 
````css
.reveal .sourceCode {
    overflow: visible;
}
````
needed for the line numbering by Pandoc to work - It was introduced in Quarto in the PR at first but now it is included in Pandoc template. However, this mess up with scrolling as discussed in the PR #147 and we never put back support. It conflicted with the scrolling that should be on each fragmented `<code>` element for the scrolling detection to work. 

Correct fix seems to be more precise as we are doing in Quarto targetting the div only
https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/a8e82471fde620f848bd6e21e98a069a41ce71d7/src/resources/formats/revealjs/styles.html#L3-L6

So for now I am patching the template by removing the rule, as we already have it ourselves before Pandoc included it 

I'll PR a fix in Pandoc also as I think this is still an issue for them. On our side I think it is ok. At least the example works fine now with scrolling and we still get the line numbers

````markdown
            sliderInput("bins",
                        "Number of bins:",
                        min = 1,
                        max = 50,
                        value = 30)
        ),

        # Show a plot of the generated distribution
        mainPanel(
           plotOutput("distPlot")
        )
    )
)

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
server <- function(input, output) {

    output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
        # generate bins based on input$bins from ui.R
        x    <- faithful[, 2]
        bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1)

        # draw the histogram with the specified number of bins
        hist(x, breaks = bins, col = 'darkgray', border = 'white')
    })
}

# Create the shiny app
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
````

title: use dash (-) rather than dot (.) to delimit fig/layout/code chunk options
description:
All of the Pandoc and Quarto document level YAML options use the pandoc convention of separating multiple words with dashes (e.g. `section-numbers`, `highlight-style`, `toc-float`, etc.). In spite of this, we initially adopted the convention of using dot (.) as the separator for some chunk options (e.g. `fig.cap`, `layout.ncol`). 

This was based on Knitr conventions, which were in turn a consequence of the fact that R symbols can't have an embedded dash unless they are quoted with backticks (e.g. `` `toc-float` = TRUE``), and Knitr chunk options are parsed as R code.

However, this creates some unfortunate inconsistency as users now need to remember when dash is used and when dot is used, and to avoid this confusion in some cases we dropped the prefix from the chunk option. For example, the global YAML options `code-fold` and `code-summary` were mapped to chunk options `fold` and `summary`(the alternative being changing the global YAML options to `fold` and `summary` which is insufficient scoping/namespacing, or changing both global and chunk options to `code.fold` / `code.summary` (which is completely inconsistent with the dash convention used by other options).

Now that Quarto chunk options are specified in YAML format, we have the opportunity to make this completely consistent (use the dash format everywhere). The only major downside of this is that Knitr users migrating to Quarto might still want to use the dot syntax. To mitigate this we do two things:

1) Continue allowing Knitr chunk options to be specified on the top line in R format (using dot notation)
2) Automatically map any `fig.` options provided in YAML to `fig-` (so for Knitr users either syntax is supported).

We will exclusively document the dash syntax, and the dot syntax will be there only as a fallback for Knitr users accustomed to using dot.

This change affects the following chunk options:


| Original      | Revised       |
|---------------|---------------|
| fig.cap       | fig-cap       |
| fig.subcap    | fig-subcap    |
| fig.scap      | fig-scap      |
| fig.link      | fig-link      |
| fig.align     | fig-align     |
| fig.env       | fig-env       |
| fig.pos       | fig-pos       |
| fig.alt       | fig-alt       |
| fold          | code-fold     |
| summary       | code-summary  |
| layout.nrow   | layout-nrow   |
| layout.ncol   | layout-ncol   |
| layout.align  | layout-align  |
| layout.valign | layout-valign |
| lst.label     | lst-label     |
| lst.cap       | lst-cap       |
| out.width     | out-width     |
| out.height    | out-height    |

title: Add a fig-responsive execute option
description:
This is defaulting to TRUE for HTML bootstrap format only. This will mean no responsiveness for htmlwidgets in revealjs format in 
R

Adding `fig-responsive` as an execute option means that the new assignment of `htmlwidgets:::resolveSizing()` happens conditionally if the option is TRUE. Changes are done in `patch.R` and `execute.R`. 

Then `fig-responsive` default to FALSE for HTML bootstrap was trickier. Doing this meant to be able to set `format.execute["fig-responsive"] = TRUE` only for bootstrap format. In order to do that, I added a `executeFilter` following the logic of `metadataFilter` to be able to modify `execute` default option based on metadata set by the user. In our case the `theme` metadata defining is the format is Bootstrap HTML or not. I did not used `formatHasBootstrap()` because I was not sure how to use from within the format creation itself.  I did this logic for setting the default value conditionally to the theme metadata. 

@jjallaire I am opening this PR so that you can check the logic considering our previous discussion (I did not see how this would have fit in `bootstrapExtras` )

I need to tweak to not make it responsive if user has change the figure sizes.

Bug #1609 has a number of great suggestions for improving citation metadata for documents. This addresses most of those suggestions, generating additional `citation_` meta tags based upon document citation data as well as making our handling of citation data more consistent.

We will newly output:
`citation_abstract`
`citation_doi`
`citation_pmid`
`citation_language`
`citation_keywords`
`citation_pdf_url`
`citation_public_url`
`citation_abstract_url`
`citation_fulltext_url`
`citation_journal_abbrev`
`citation_publisher`

Based upon the `type` specified:
`citation_conference_title`/`citation_conference`
`citation_dissertation_institution`
`citation_book_title`

General approach is to allow specification of citation data with names and structure that corresponds with CSL schema and to map those values onto the appropriate meta names (rather than matching the meta names directly).

title: Invalid href when output-file contains a ‘.’ in its name
description:
If the output the output file is simple, like:

```
output-file: test
```

we automatically would generate the output file `test.html`.

but if the `output-file` contains a `.`, then we would not append the extension (thinking that it already had one), resulting in a case like:

```
output-file: file.name
```

producing a file named `file.name` rather than `file.name.html`.

This will amend the behavior do the appending for any file without an extension or if the appending won’t result in duplicate extensions (e.g. `file.html.html`).

title: Ensure that cache returns a copy
description:
When reading an extension from the cache, we need to be sure to return a copy of the object. This is because downstream, the object could be mutated (in this case, paths are resolved on the object itself). When the cache wasn’t returning a copy, the cached object would be mutated by the first path resolution, and subsequent path resolutions would fail (since the resolved path was now stored in the cache).

Fixes #1361

title: Adapt regex to correctly match table environments in LaTeX
description:
Fixes #1093

It seems like I need to use special `.-` pattern to match correctly the table environment part. 

<details>
<summary>Qmd file </summary>

````markdown
---
title: "test"
format: pdf
keep-tex: true
keep-md: true
---

```{r}
#| label: tbl-one
#| tbl-cap: "A table"
#| echo: fenced

mtcars[1:2,] |> tibble::rownames_to_column() |> gt::gt(rowname_col = "rowname")
```

````

</details>

**gt** produces the following table
````latex
\captionsetup[table]{labelformat=empty,skip=1pt}
\begin{longtable}{r|rrrrrrrrrrr}
\toprule
\multicolumn{1}{l}{} & mpg & cyl & disp & hp & drat & wt & qsec & vs & am & gear & carb \\ 
\midrule
Mazda RX4 & 21 & 6 & 160 & 110 & 3.9 & 2.620 & 16.46 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 4 \\ 
Mazda RX4 Wag & 21 & 6 & 160 & 110 & 3.9 & 2.875 & 17.02 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 4 \\ 
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
````

And Quarto was inserting in the wrong place causing issue in LaTeX
````latex
\hypertarget{tbl-one}{}
\captionsetup[table]{labelformat=empty,skip=1pt}
\begin{longtable}{r|rrrrrrrrrrr}
\toprule
\multicolumn{1}{l}{}
\caption{\label{tbl-one}A table }\tabularnewline
 & mpg & cyl & disp & hp & drat & wt & qsec & vs & am & gear & carb \\ 
\midrule
Mazda RX4 & 21 & 6 & 160 & 110 & 3.9 & 2.620 & 16.46 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 4 \\ 
Mazda RX4 Wag & 21 & 6 & 160 & 110 & 3.9 & 2.875 & 17.02 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 4 \\ 
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
````

Changing the regex correctly place the table after `\begin{longtable}{r|rrrrrrrrrrr}`

````latex
\hypertarget{tbl-one}{}
\captionsetup[table]{labelformat=empty,skip=1pt}
\begin{longtable}{r|rrrrrrrrrrr}
\caption{\label{tbl-one}A table }\tabularnewline

\toprule
\multicolumn{1}{l}{} & mpg & cyl & disp & hp & drat & wt & qsec & vs & am & gear & carb \\ 
\midrule
Mazda RX4 & 21 & 6 & 160 & 110 & 3.9 & 2.620 & 16.46 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 4 \\ 
Mazda RX4 Wag & 21 & 6 & 160 & 110 & 3.9 & 2.875 & 17.02 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 4 \\ 
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
````

title: [Windows] Improve R finding for special installation
description:
This fixes #995

After some tests with R installation with Scoop and rig on Windows, here are some ajustement in what we are doing.
With this change:  
* Scoop or rig installation will be found when in terminal for PATH or registry version
* They will also be found inside RStudio where `R_HOME` is set and takes precedence. 

For `scoop`, as described in #995, the installation will not add a `Rscript.exe` file in `R_HOME/bin`, they will be in `R_HOME/bin/x64` only. I kept the adjustment simple for now by adding directly the path to `x64` folder if none is found in root `bin` folder. This is really scoped to the specific issue. If we want more generic approach, it could be clever to search for the `Rscript.exe` within the `R_HOME` folder and take the first one found. Could be done by refactoring the search in program files 
https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/abb46a31904665e3774319520e7d8473c869290d/src/core/resources.ts#L97-L106
If needed, I'll add that. 

For `rig`, it took me more time to test because I found a few issues that messed up my system; They are reported in https://github.com/r-lib/rig.  It helps though identified one thing: `which()` uses `CMD /C WHERE <binary>`. This command on windows will return all the files found, and not just the only one like `which` on Linux.  I added a handling of this: we are keeping only the first path returned. 

Regarding search in registry, , I noticed a few things that I was not sure : 

* Is there a reason to no read the version install path in two steps ? 
https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/abb46a31904665e3774319520e7d8473c869290d/src/core/resources.ts#L76-L93
`Software\\R-core\\R` as a `InstallPath` value directly. So I was wondering by curiosity. I did not change anything as this is working fine currently. 

* Slightly unrelated, we have two sets of registry reading functions: in `registry.ts` and in `windows.ts`. Should we try refactor into one set for easier upkeep in the future ? Asking because I fixed one issue in the past in `windows.ts` for chrome finding, but not the other that I wasn't aware of.

title: use host in preview and serve
description:
The documentation website of [Viash](https://viash.io) urgently needs a makeover, and I was looking into using quarto to create it. However, I ran into the issue of the `--host` parameter not being passed along inside of the code. This means I can't access the web server from inside a container.

## Demonstration of the issue

I set up a new website. For this example, I'll be using Viash to make the Docker container build a little bit easier:

```bash
quarto create-project mysite --type website
cd mysite

# download viash
mkdir bin
wget https://github.com/viash-io/viash/releases/download/0.5.11/viash -O bin/viash
chmod +x viash
```
I created a [Viash component](https://github.com/rcannood/quarto-cli/blob/viash_configs/src/viash_configs/quarto_preview/config.vsh.yaml) (which is a script + a description of the CLI + a Docker container spec) to make running quarto preview easier.

When I run the Viash component, I get:

```bash
$ bin/viash run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rcannood/quarto-cli/viash_configs/src/viash_configs/quarto_preview/config.vsh.yaml
```

    [notice] Checking if Docker image is available at 'quarto_preview:latest'
    [warning] Could not pull from 'quarto_preview:latest'. Docker image doesn't exist or is not accessible.
    [notice] Building container 'quarto_preview:latest' with Dockerfile
    
    Preparing to preview
    
    Watching files for changes
    Browse at http://localhost:4444/


When I try to browse `http://localhost:4444/`, it fails because the web server is bound to 127.0.0.1.

## Demonstration of the solution

This [Viash component](https://github.com/rcannood/quarto-cli/blob/viash_configs/src/viash_configs/quarto_preview_fix/config.vsh.yaml) uses my fork of quarto.

This time, I will build the component explicitly into an executable. The Docker container build will take a bit longer because it's building quarto from source.

```bash
viash build https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rcannood/quarto-cli/viash_configs/src/viash_configs/quarto_preview_fixed/config.vsh.yaml -o bin --setup cachedbuild
```
    [notice] Building container 'quarto_preview_fix:latest' with Dockerfile

When I run the Viash component, I get:
```bash
# need to clean up previous preview first
bin/quarto_preview_fix
```

    Terminating existing preview server....DONE

```bash
bin/quarto_preview_fix
```
    Preparing to preview
    
    Watching files for changes
    Browse at http://172.17.0.2:4444/

Browsing this link now works.

Sidenote: The executable generated by Viash now works as a standalone executable which uses a Docker container in the backend.

This PR adds a a lua-filter which allows the following syntax:

````

Hello from the digital version.
:::

:::print-only
Hello from the print version.
:::
````

title: Correctly query registry key on Windows for finding chrome
description:
Fix #868

There was 2 issues: 
1. Quoting issue with `Deno.run()` as we encountered with `tlmgr` in the past
2. Localized output value of `reg.exe query` which made our regex matching failed

For the first, I refactored the fix for `tlmgr` by making the wrapper `safeWindowsExec` available in `windows.ts` so that we can reuse it. Basically the trick is to quote the arguments that needs it (`requireQuoting()`), then write the command to execute into a `.bat` file using `Deno.run()`

For the second, I understand we don't need to search for `Default` in the returned key when `/ve` is used on the query as only the default will be returned. So when `(Default)` keyname issued, we ignore it in the regex. 

This solve the issue on Windows. Hopefully, it is not breaking anything elsewhere. 

Side notes: 

I took some time before submitting the PR as we discussed with @dragonstyle making the quoting on Windows more generic as this is a known issue with `Deno.run()`. Idea was to make `execProcess()` supports this. However, it is a bit more complex that I though and this seems to lead to change the way `execProcess()` is called, and we use that in a lot of places. 

That is only the second time we are encountering this and we now have a pattern using `requireQuoting()` and then `safeExecWindows()` when needed. Maybe that is enough for now ? 
Anyway, I could still continue this rewrite, but it would probably be good in another PR.

This will close #877 We were too generic in our approach of detecting single in slides and moving it to
level with class `r-stretch` added. This would break images set in custom divs. With this change, we are doing `auto-stretch` only for setup we know that should work. See https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/877#issuecomment-1127435945 for details. Those setup are all at `
` level already; 1. Single image in slides not nested under any structure 2. image with caption, that will be in Quarto figure divs 3. image created from Code cells, which will be in special divs If any of the above is nested under something else (like with custom class divs), we don't apply auto-stretch, unless the first level divs has `r-stretch` class on it. In that case, the img in the div will be unwrapped **and put below the custom div**. As before, special div for Quarto feature are ignored: layout, columns, fragments, output-location, ... I added some tests for this support, which shows an example presentation. Is this now the expected behavior ?

title: Improve support of specific knitr engines for source output
description:
it should not be pass through so that it does not end up into the div when pass as a knitr option. 

This option is new from knitr 1.38 (https://github.com/yihui/knitr/blob/master/NEWS.md#changes-in-knitr-version-138)

I don't think this option `lang` has any effect in Quarto yet. So we have a difference in behavior between **knitr** in R Markdown and in Quarto. 

With **knitr**, `lang` is used in various place to change the language that will be applied as class to the code chunk in Markdown. Default is the engine. Sometimes it needs to be tweaked.

Example: 

````markdown
```{verbatim, lang = "js"}
console.log('test')
```
````

This is used in **knitr** to output a code chunk of class `js`

````markdown
```{bash, lang = "default"}
pwd
```
````

This is used to execute a chunk as bash but highlight as a default block. 


So this PR only makes sure that the option is correctly identified a knitr option. I'll make another one (or just continue in this one if you prefer) to make the recent engine (`verbatim`, `embed`, `comment`, ...) works correctly. They are not really working as expected I believe (mainly because we overwrite the source hook I think).

title: Use "セクション" to the prefix for sections in Japanese
description:
The current Japanese translation uses the prefix `章` instead of `Section` when referring to a section. For example, `章 1.2.3`.
However, this is not a common expression. Generally, `章` is a suffix, not a prefix, and the most natural way to express this is `第1章第2節第3項`.

Since it is difficult to perform such a translation with the current translation function, it would be better to use `セクション` like `セクション 1.2.3`.

title: Fix hostname addr type convertation and update info output
description:
## Information for help:

- `quarto-cli` version: 0.9.39 (download from github release page)

## What I want to do:

I'm using `quarto` to create a project in my **remote server** and write my documents. Then I hope to use `quarto` to host and preview generated website. I try to specify a public address as hostname to preview arguments, which I could browse site from my **local laptop**. But I found it does't work and show the wrong url path.

```
$ quarto preview --port 4485 --host 0.0.0.0 --no-navigate --no-browser
Preparing to preview

Watching files for changes
Browse at http://localhost:4485/
```

## What I found:

After my debugging, I found `quarto` preview subcommod didn't [recognize host correctly](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/12abf43f89b39ffa36404842ad09a04b8cba5e16/src/command/preview/cmd.ts#L162). And url output `printBrowsePreviewMessage` has no hostname passed.

## What I did:

1. Replace `parseInt` with `String` when parsing arguments
2. Add a new arg `host` to function `printBrowsePreviewMessage()` and update all codes called `printBrowsePreviewMessage()`
3. [Modified but reverted] Update `http://localhost:${options.port}/` to `http://${options.host}:${options.port}/`, but later I realized this is used for opening local browser, so I reverted back again.

That's all, thx

title: Add translations for de
description:
I agree with @yitao-li and @cderv that this is surprisingly difficult (not knowing the pragmatic context).

At least I had the advantage of being able to base my translation on two languages already (unfortunately, not knowing Mandarin).


### Questions/comments:
 
1.

Sometimes, I'm using punctuation, to more strongly convey the intention. For example:

```
callout-important-caption: "Wichtig!"
callout-danger-caption: "Achtung! Gefährlich!"
```

This assumes these are tooltips - which should be correct, right? - but should be fine even if not. 

However, these:

```
search-matching-documents-text: "Gefundene Dokumente:"
search-more-match-text: "Weitere Ergebnisse in diesem Dokument:"
search-more-matches-text: "Weitere Ergebnisse in diesem Dokument:"
```

assume that these are headings, or just text, but not tooltips, for example. (Such that the colons make sense.)
Is this assumption correct?


2. 
I agree with @cderv that the difference between these:

search-more-match-text
search-more-matches-text

is not clear. Perhaps we're misunderstanding something? (I followed @cderv in taking both as meaning the same, but perhaps that's not intended?) 

3.

I left the prefixes as-is, as I don't know of any common abbreviations for those anyway (in German even less than in English :-)).

title: Get images, alignement and caption before removing any element
description:
This follows #231 and #224. There was a mix in the process for images with no caption - the quarto figure container was removed before the alignement value was picked up and put on the moved `` It could be the source of the report in https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/pull/231#issuecomment-998496713 by @JulianTao This PR changes the order. One the image and its main container is found, we 1. Check if there is a figure environment and if so, 2. Get the alignement value to put on the `` 3. Get a caption if any Then 4. we remove the image from its node and delete its empty parent if any 5. We move it to the first level 6. we add the `

` caption just below 7. we remove the whole figure container if still one It seems better ordered this way.

title: Automatically add stretch class on images when only one in slides
description:
This PR is leveraging the stretch feature from revealjs: https://revealjs.com/layout/#stretch ## Current Status Sharing this so that we can discuss and you can test. ## Idea Automatically apply the strech class on images when there is only one image in slides. The reveal feature is normally based on adding the class manually to the image, and currently only one image can be stretch per slide. The plan is to use a post process of the HTML to modify the HTML code so that reveal process can apply as expected. ## How it works for reveal ? reveal will apply a transformation when `Reveal.layout()` for this stretch class https://github.com/hakimel/reveal.js/blob/b7d65be051072c4f36334403f0cdc19f88ce09c3/js/reveal.js#L954 * Detect any **direct child** of `
` with the class `stretch` (or `r-streched`) * Calculate remaining Height * Apply to the element using inline style attributes ## How image works in Quarto ? Pandoc has a specific detection and process for img of class `stretch`. Usually non caption `` are put inside a `

` as any other element in Pandoc, and caption image inside a figure element (`implicit_figure` extension), but when class stretch is there, pandoc will put the `` first level, completely not considering the caption. Quarto will do as pandoc for non captioned, but will have its own process for figure environment putting the img into a div, keeping the caption in `

title: fix configuration for symlink bin directories
description:
Calling `ensureDirSync` on `"/home/user/bin"` for example will fail if `bin` is a symlink to a directory (because it's a file). Calling it on `"/home/user/bin/"` (by appending a path separator) will force resolving the link so bin is seen as a directory (if the link target is a directory). This mechanism is described at https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/path_resolution.7.html 

This fixes the build on my computer where `~/bin` is a symlink.

title: reveal: Default to slide level 2 and allow vertical navigation only when navigationMode is changed
description:
Following discussion, this PR has changed purposed.  A very small PR after all

This sets slide-level to be 2 by default, meaning with this example
````
---
title: demo reveal
output: revealjs
---

# Section Header

## Header on vertical slide

Content on verticle slide

# Section header 

With content 

## Another slide 

will be vertical in reveal. 
````

We would have 
1. A title slide
2. A section title slide
3. A slide with content
4. A section title slide with content
5. A slide with content

Activating overview would show the vertical slides but `navigationMode: linear` would prevent a vertical navigation. 

To activate verticals controls, one would have to do `navigationMode: default`. This would not change the content, but add the controls and right arrow would only show section titles.

Is this a good new default ? Only usage could tell us. While documenting the feature we could change our decision. 

From my tests, other useful value for revealjs are: 

* `slide-level: 0` : only `---` would create slides
* `slide-level: 1`: Slide would be created only with header 1 
* `slide-level` > 2 : would be a very bad idea with revealJS as it would create normal slide for the slide level only. This would only be useful when a upper level is never used. e.g `slide-level: 3` when only `##` for section and `###` for slides is used. Not sure it should happen.

title: Add process to update reveal.js in `update-html-dependencies`
description:
At first I did it to update on a github release tag but it seems a commit is better.
Other example on commit is for Bootstrap  and it is using `git`. I think we can do without GIT and did it accordingly for reveal.js. 

this is also in light of an issue discussed with @dragonstyle where on Windows `Deno.removeSync` does not manage to clean a folder cloned using Git. (because of Git access right on filesytem were read only files are created). 
This lead to adding Try Catch so the the scripts runs on Windows without terminating early due to error.

Regarding the reveal.js update: 

* We get `css/`, `dist/` and `plugin/`
* We remove unwanted `.css` in the `dist/theme/` folder

I choose to update the existing `updateGithubSourceCodeDependency()` function to support a commit in addition of a release tag. I used a new optional `commit` argument set to `false` by default. Another idea was do detect if the env var was a git commit or a version number using for example `.` detection as commit won't have any dots usually. It could be on the number of character too. Anyway, tell me if this is a better idea.

If the process seems valid, I could also change the way we get the bootstrap deps to use the same zip download. This would avoid using Git and would avoid the "Permission Denied" issue on Windows.

title: docs: runtime migration plans (move quarto-cli off Deno)
description:
## Description

Planning record for moving quarto-cli off Deno onto Node, as documentation only. No application code, no build change. It adds `dev-docs/runtime-migration/`: the decision record, the validating spike, two reviews with their triage, and one self-contained implementation plan per PR across four phases.

The work is organized as 45 PRs plus two time-boxed spikes and one upstream milestone (the Julia engine, ported by PumasAI), executed one at a time against `main`:

- Phase 0, de-risk dependencies: a CI ratchet counting `Deno.*` call sites and direct std imports (PR 02), the Deno 2.9 bump and a committed `--frozen` lockfile, and swapping `deno.land/x`/skypack/cliffy/deno_dom dependencies for npm/jsr equivalents.
- Phase 1, close the runtime boundary: route every `Deno.*` and std import through a new `src/deno_ral/` layer, via mechanical codemods, while still shipping on Deno.
- Phase 2, Node implementations, still on Deno: build the Node versions of the layer's modules behind a real-Node CI job with a shrink-only known-failures list. Two spikes settle Deno/Node compatibility and the test runner.
- Phase 3, flip then remove Deno: switch the CLI launchers to Node (with a one-cycle dual-runtime window if the spike passes), move user scripts and `build-ts-extension`, then stop downloading Deno.

`README.md` is the execution index (the ordered PR table, dependency graph, ground rules, roles, release calendar). `HANDOFF.md` is the start-here for a fresh session. Every plan carries its own spec, files, checkbox tasks, verification commands, risks, and a suggested executor.

Merging this first puts the plans on `main` so each implementation PR can branch from `main` and reference them. The first plan to execute is PR 02 (the runtime-boundary ratchet). Its baseline numbers are re-measured against the merge-base at execution time, since `main` has moved since the plans were written.

No user-facing change, so no changelog line and no website PR.

title: Fix light/dark toggle shown when the dark brand file is ignored
description:
Since #15101, a brand file that holds only comments is ignored with a warning. When that file is the `dark` one of a light/dark brand, the HTML page still got the color-scheme toggle with no dark stylesheet to switch to. With only `brand: {dark: ...}`, the page also started in dark mode (`body.quarto-dark`) with the light styles.

## Root cause

Whether a page has a dark mode comes from `darkModeDefault()` in `src/format/html/format-html-info.ts`, which reads the key order of `theme:` and `brand:` in the metadata. Once the dark file is dropped, the `brand:` metadata still lists `dark:`, so the check reports a dark mode the loaded brand does not have. The same predicate gates the website navbar toggle, dashboards, giscus and the brand Sass defaults.

## Fix

`brand:` key order now counts only when a dark brand was actually loaded (`format.render.brand.dark`). `theme:` key order is still checked first, so `theme: {light, dark}` keeps its toggle when the dark brand file is ignored. `darkModeDefaultMetadata()` keeps its behavior, as `render-contexts.ts` calls it before the brand is loaded.

Each new smoke-all document has its own comment-only fixture. The warning goes through `warnOnce`, so documents sharing one file in the same test run would see it only once.

Fixes #15131

title: Support Quarto 2's div syntax for definition lists
description:
## Description

Adds support for Quarto 2's div syntax for definition lists, so authors can move to it while still on Quarto 1, ahead of a migration:

````md
::: {.definition-list}
* `time`
  - A timestamp that identifies when the request was initiated.
  - Type: string
* `id`
  - A unique identifier.
:::
````

Each top-level bullet is a term, and the bullets nested under it are its definitions. Quarto 2 doesn't support Pandoc's `term` / `: definition` syntax, and this is what it uses instead.

This follows the `list-table` precedent (#13528):

- New module `src/resources/filters/modules/definitionlist.lua`, registered in `_quarto.modules`.
- New `astpipeline-process-definition-lists` pass in `normalize/astpipeline.lua`, right after the list-table pass, so it runs before crossrefs and user filters.

The structural rules match Quarto 2's (`is_valid_definition_list_div` / `transform_definition_list_div` in pampa):

- The div contains exactly one bullet list.
- Each item is a term (`Plain` or `Para`) followed by a nested bullet list of definitions.
- A div with any other shape is left as is, without a warning.
- The div's id, classes and attributes are dropped, since `DefinitionList` has no `Attr`.

Like `listtable.lua`, it skips the `data-pos` wrapper divs added by the `sourcepos` extension.

No `flags` gate: `compute_flags` runs after the AST pipeline, so a flag couldn't skip this pass (the same reason `has_list_tables` is set but unused).

### Open questions

1. **Malformed divs.** `list-table` stops the render with an error; Quarto 2 leaves a malformed `.definition-list` div alone silently. This PR matches Quarto 2. A warning in Quarto 1 could help people learning the syntax, but would flag what Quarto 2 accepts.
2. **Dropped attributes.** `::: {#foo .definition-list}` loses `#foo`, as in Quarto 2. Keeping it would mean wrapping the list in a `Div`, which differs from Quarto 2.

### Testing

- New smoke test `tests/docs/smoke-all/markdown/definition-list/definition-list-div.qmd`, with `html`, `latex` and `typst` checks for tight, loose and nested lists and for malformed divs staying divs.
- I checked the module directly with pandoc 3.12.1 (pandoc markdown, and commonmark with `+sourcepos`), and rendered the test document with a dev `quarto` pointed at this branch's filters through `QUARTO_SHARE_PATH`; the `html`, `latex` and `typst` assertions match that output.
- I have not yet run `./run-tests.sh` on this test or the wider suite.

title: Fix code copy button and spacing for code blocks at callout edges
description:
Since #13024 wrapped code blocks in `div.code-copy-outer-scaffold` (first released in v1.8.15), a code block that starts or ends a callout has its copy button above the code frame, half outside it, and gets much more space than a paragraph at the same edge.

Stacked on #15136 (#13444), which it needs for annotated code blocks in callouts. It should be merged after it.

## Root cause

The callout edge rules in `_bootstrap-rules.scss` were written for `div.sourceCode`, but the edge child is now the scaffold, or a `.cell` around it.

- The `0.5rem` padding of `.callout-body > :first-child` and `:last-child` lands on the scaffold. It stops the `1em` margin of `div.sourceCode` from collapsing, so the code moves down while the button stays at `top: 0` of the scaffold.
- `:last-child:not(.sourceCode)` was meant to exempt code blocks, but the scaffold is not `.sourceCode`.
- The `> div > :last-child` branch now matches the copy button itself, which gets an extra `padding-bottom`.

## Fix

At a callout edge, the scaffold (or a cell whose edge child is the scaffold) gets the spacing as margin instead of padding, and `div.sourceCode` drops its own margin there. The button is back 5px inside the code frame, and code at the edge gets the same spacing as a paragraph in the same callout. The copy button is excluded from the `> div > :last-child` rule. The rules are based on the CSS suggested in the issue thread.

The cell rules use `:has()` to only apply when code is at the edge of the cell, so a cell ending with its output keeps its current spacing.

This is a visible change compared to 1.7, where the callout padding applied to `div.sourceCode` itself, so the code frame was flush to the callout header (#13238). #13238 also asks to change padding to margin for other first children of a callout, which changes more than code blocks, so it is not part of this PR.

Moving the margin onto the scaffold for every code block was considered, as the same offset happens in sections using the column grid (#15137). That rule adds 17px of space in tabsets and between a filename header and its code, as these contexts reset the margin on `div.sourceCode`, and the callout edge rules would still be needed. The grid case is tracked separately in #15137.

No backport is planned: the regression is from v1.8.15 and the stable release is v1.10.

Fixes #13446

title: Fix code copy button covering code annotation marker
description:
Since #13024 wrapped the code copy button in `div.code-copy-outer-scaffold` (first released in v1.8.15), the button no longer sits inside the `pre`.
The rule that moved it clear of the annotation gutter, `.code-annotated .code-copy-button`, still targets a descendant of `pre.code-annotated`, so it matches nothing.
On an annotated block the button lands on top of the marker on the first line, and the annotation can no longer be opened by hover or click.

## Fix

The selector now follows the scaffold: `.code-copy-outer-scaffold:has(pre.code-annotated) > .code-copy-button`.
The scaffold itself stays, as it is what keeps the button from scrolling with the code and lets line numbers work (#13009, #5538).
The rule is based on the one suggested in the issue thread.

The old `1.25em` margin worked in 1.7 because the button sat inside the `pre` and inherited the code font size.
The button now has the body font size, while the gutter is `calc(20px + 0.5em)` in the code font size.
The rule therefore sets `font-size: $code-block-font-size` on the button, so `margin-right: calc(20px + 0.5em + 5px)` is the gutter width plus the button's usual 5px for any theme font size.
It is written with `em` rather than `0.5 * $code-block-font-size`, because a percentage value such as `75%` would resolve against the container width inside `margin` and push the button far into the code.

Annotated blocks inside callouts are still wrong, which is separate and tracked in #13446.
No backport is planned: the regression is from v1.8.15 and the stable release is v1.10.

Fixes #13444

title: fix: only skip hidden paths below the walked directory
description:
🤖:

---

Fixes #3186

If any directory above a project's root starts with a dot, for example `~/.julia/dev/MyPackage/docs` or a git worktree under `.claude/worktrees/`, Quarto doesn't treat the documents in it as part of the project. There is no error: `quarto render` of the project does nothing, and rendering a single document from it silently ignores `_quarto.yml` metadata, project extensions etc.

The cause is that `kSkipHidden` (`/[/\\][\.]/`) was matched against the absolute paths that `walk` yields, including the walk root itself. So the project ends up with no input files, `projectContext()` doesn't find the rendered file among them and falls back to a single-file context.

The docs say hidden files and folders are ignored "in the project directory", and the relative-path ignore globs in `projectInputFiles` already only look below the root, so the match above the root looks unintended. This replaces the constant with `skipHiddenWithin(dir)`, which only matches dot components below the directory being walked. Hidden files and folders inside the project (`.git`, `.venv`, `.hidden/d.qmd`) are still skipped and still pruned from the walk. The other users of `kSkipHidden` (extension file watching, MECA bundles, `projectYamlFiles`) had the same problem and are switched over too.

title: Fix revealjs tabset keyboard focus order
description:
In `revealjs`, tabset tabs and the focusable content of their panels get positive `tabindex` values (`1`, `2`, ...). Positive values come before every other element in the Tab order, so a link placed before a tabset on a slide is reached only after all the tabs and their content. Each tabset also counts from `1`, so two tabsets on the same slide are visited interleaved.

The symptom first reported in #14970, <kbd>Tab</kbd> on an earlier slide reaching a tab on a later one, was #14795 and is fixed by #15010. #15007 brought back upstream tabby behavior outside `revealjs` (#730) and fixed <kbd>Home</kbd>/<kbd>End</kbd> also changing slide. What remains is the order within a slide, fixed here.

## Root cause

Our copy of tabby was changed in 2021 so that arrow keys keep moving slides in `revealjs`: tabs are selected as soon as they get focus, and all tabs are in the Tab order. As tabs come before all panels in the DOM, <kbd>Tab</kbd> then goes from tab to tab and the content of a panel is not reachable. The increasing `tabindex` values were added to get back the order tab A, content of A, tab B, content of B.

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/83097c10af6bc5dd50a79b66739f1e34843ee3fb/src/resources/formats/html/tabby/js/tabby.js#L315-L336

## Fix

Tabs keep `tabindex="0"` and arrow keys still change slides. The same order now comes from handling <kbd>Tab</kbd> on tabs and panels: <kbd>Tab</kbd> on a tab goes to the first focusable element of its panel, and from the last one to the next tab. <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> goes the other way, selecting the previous tab first. Anything else is left to the browser, so focus enters and leaves the tabset in document order.

<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> from content after a tabset would reach the selected panel first and skip the tabs after it. In that case the last tab is selected and focus starts from the end of its panel, so going backwards is the reverse of going forwards. Clicks don't trigger this.

The first and last focusable elements of a panel have to match what the browser actually focuses: `summary` and not `details` (folded code), not hidden content, not links in fragments not yet shown (`visibility: hidden`), and not controls disabled by their `fieldset`. When a panel ends with a nested tabset, its end is the end of that tabset's last panel. A control that handles <kbd>Tab</kbd> itself, like a code editor, keeps it.

Alternative considered: a roving `tabindex` with arrow keys switching tabs, the ARIA tabs pattern used outside `revealjs` since #15007. It was not used because clicking a tab leaves focus on it, so a presenter using arrow keys or a clicker would switch tabs instead of slides. This was asked on the issue without feedback.

Fixes #14970

title: Use one focus ring for all focusable elements in Bootstrap HTML
description:
## Description Closes #15139. Supersedes #14867. Quarto's HTML output uses four different keyboard focus indicators. Two of them fail the 3:1 contrast minimum of WCAG 1.4.11. In forced-colors mode, some controls have no focus indicator at all. The issue gives the details and measurements. This PR replaces the four indicators with one focus ring, defined in one place. ### The ring One rule, `:focus-visible` in `_bootstrap-rules.scss`, draws the ring for every focusable element. The ring follows [W3C technique C40](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/css/C40): two tones with at least 9:1 contrast between them. As a result, one of the two tones has at least 3:1 contrast against any solid background. - The outer tone is a 2px `outline`, with `outline-offset: 2px`. - The inner tone is a `box-shadow` of 2px that fills the offset. The outer tone is on the `outline` for two reasons. Bootswatch themes often set `box-shadow` on controls, but they rarely set `outline`. Forced-colors mode also keeps the `outline` and removes the `box-shadow`. `default`: `cosmo` (e.g. used on quarto.org): ### Tone order follows the page The two tones are white and a dark tone, derived from `$primary-text-emphasis`. On a light page, the dark tone is the outer ring. On a dark page, the tones change places, so the white tone is the outer ring. Thus the outer ring always contrasts with the page. A page is dark if `$body-bg` has more contrast with white than with black. In the built-in themes, seven themes are dark: cyborg, darkly, quartz, slate, solar, superhero, and vapor. `cyborg`: `darkly`: ### Contrast between the tones The derived pair always has at least 9:1 contrast, in all themes: - In the default theme and all 25 Bootswatch themes, `$primary-text-emphasis` already has at least 9:1 contrast against white. The lowest is minty, at 9.13:1. The highest is lux, at 19.80:1. - A user theme can have a lighter `$primary`, which gives less than 9:1. In this case, Quarto darkens the derived tone only as much as necessary to get 9:1. For example, `$primary: #ffd54f` goes from 7.26:1 to 9.16:1. ### How authors change the ring Users can set the two tones with `$focus-ring-outer-color` and `$focus-ring-inner-color`. If a user sets one or both variables, Quarto uses the colors as given: - Quarto does not change the tone order on dark pages. - Quarto does not adjust an explicit outer color to get 9:1. If a user sets only the inner color, Quarto still derives the outer color and adjusts it to 9:1 against the inner color. Users can set the size of the ring with `$focus-ring-outline-width` and `$focus-ring-outline-offset` (both 2px by default). The inner tone always fills the offset. Quarto adds padding to scroll containers from these two values, so a larger ring is not clipped. A width of less than 2px does not meet WCAG 2.4.13. Author focus rules still win over the ring: - The global rule has specificity (0,1,0). Author rules such as `a:focus-visible` (0,1,1) win over it. Many sites have rules like this one. - The inner tone is `box-shadow: var(--quarto-focus-ring-shadow)`. Most author rules set only `outline`, so the inner tone stays inside the author ring. To remove it, add `--quarto-focus-ring-shadow: none` to the author rule or to `:root`. Quarto no longer uses Bootstrap's `$focus-ring-color`, `$focus-ring-box-shadow`, `$btn-focus-width`, and `$btn-focus-box-shadow`. The changelog tells authors to use the new variables and the custom property instead. ### Other changes - Bootstrap's focus halos are off at the source: `$focus-ring-box-shadow`, `$form-select-focus-box-shadow`, and `$form-range-thumb-focus-box-shadow` are `none`, and `$btn-focus-width` is `0`. - The per-control focus rules are removed: the sidebar toggle rule, the `outline: revert` from #14785, and the `outline: none` rules in `quarto-search.scss`. - `accessibleContrast()` accepts a number. Also, `"A"` now gives 3:1. Before, it gave 7:1. No caller uses `"A"`. - The TOC sidebars get `padding-right: $focus-ring-extent`, so that they do not clip the ring. - The collapsed navbar menu (`.navbar-nav-scroll`) gets `padding: $focus-ring-extent` and an equal negative margin. Before, it clipped the sides of the ring. - The secondary nav gets `position: relative`, so that the top edge of the ring shows above the navbar. - The skip link (#14685) no longer has a drop shadow. Before, it needed its own focus rule to keep both the drop shadow and the inner tone. Now it gets the standard ring. ### Exceptions to "one rule" - **Bootstrap controls.** Bootstrap removes the outline with (0,2,0) rules, for example `.btn:focus-visible { outline: 0 }` and `.form-control:focus`. These rules win over the (0,1,0) global rule. A second rule includes the ring again on these classes: `.btn`, `.btn-close`, `.nav-link`, `.navbar-toggler`, `.accordion-button`, `.carousel-control-prev`, `.carousel-control-next`, `.form-control`, `.form-select`, `.form-check-input`, and `.form-range`. It ties with Bootstrap and comes later. Author rules on these classes come later again, so they still win. - **MathJax.** MathJax adds `mjx-speech:focus { outline: none }` at runtime, after the Quarto stylesheet. A `(0,2,1)` rule, `:root mjx-speech:focus-visible`, puts the ring back on each equation. - **Search box.** The visible field is `.aa-Form`, which holds a borderless `.aa-Input`. The ring goes on the form when the input has keyboard focus. - **Pagination.** vapor and zephyr give `.page-link` a `box-shadow` with a higher specificity. A `(0,4,0)` rule puts the ring back. ### Known limits - **pulse.** The theme sets `.btn:focus { outline: none }`. At 800px, the sidebar toggle and the search button have no ring, before and after this PR. I will open a separate issue. - **Theme `box-shadow` overrides.** Five themes replace the inner tone on some controls. The outer tone stays on all of them: - Tabset tab: materia, morph, quartz, zephyr. - Sidebar toggle and search button at 800px: materia, morph. - Listing sort: morph. - Listing filter: materia, morph, pulse. ### Tests and measurements All measurements come from renders and computed styles, in Chromium and WebKit. - New Playwright tests in `html-focus-indicator.spec.ts`, with the fixtures `tests/docs/playwright/website/focus-indicator/`, `tests/docs/playwright/html/focus-ring-author-override.qmd`, and `tests/docs/playwright/html/focus-ring-light-dark.qmd`. There is one test per rule that puts the ring back where Bootstrap or Quarto removed the outline (`.nav-link`, `.form-select`, `.form-control`, bare `.btn`, the sidebar toggle, the search form), plus tests for forced colors, author overrides, and the paired light/dark theme. In Chromium and WebKit, 21 tests pass and 1 test skips (forced colors is Chromium-only). On release 1.11.6, every test except the author-override test fails. - The website fixture sets `$focus-ring-outer-color`, `$focus-ring-outline-width`, and `$focus-ring-outline-offset` to values that differ from the defaults. The same assertions on every control show that the three Sass variables reach the ring. - The author-override test gives a link an `a:focus-visible` outline and `--quarto-focus-ring-shadow: none`. The test makes sure that the link shows the author outline and no inner tone. - The light/dark test asserts only that the tones swap between the two stylesheets, not the exact color each Bootswatch theme derives, so a Bootswatch update does not break it. - A Tab-key audit of 26 themes plus dark mode, at 1400px, 800px, and on a listing page: 3,189 Tab stops. 72 stops do not have the exact ring: - 54 are the search ``. This is by design, because the ring is on its form. - 16 are the theme `box-shadow` overrides above. - 2 are the pulse buttons above. - No scroll container clips the ring: the website TOC and standalone `toc-left` at 1400px and 800px, and the collapsed navbar menu at 700px. - In forced-colors mode, the navbar link, TOC link, tab, and search box had no indicator on `main`. title: Make the runtime boundary check blame only a PR's own increase
description:
Follow-up to #15135, whose absolute comparison failed every open PR after a merge race: #15134 merged 20 minutes after the ratchet, its checks had run on a base without it, and its six new `Deno.*` calls in two test files went unchecked.
`main` went red ([run](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/actions/runs/39624793470)) and, because `pull_request` runs check out the merge commit, #15136 failed for an increase it did not make ([run](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/actions/runs/39636363899)).
The baseline was raised on `main` in 8599166fb to recover.

The error text had a second problem: it always says "Application code must use src/deno_ral/", but `src/deno_ral` has no `readTextFile`, `writeTextFile`, `makeTempDir` or `env` yet, and only a thin `call()` for processes.
A bug fix that adds `Deno.readTextFileSync` in `src` failed CI with nothing to change.

Plan: [02c-ratchet-pr-delta-and-guidance.md](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/rt/02c-ratchet-pr-delta/dev-docs/runtime-migration/02c-ratchet-pr-delta-and-guidance.md)

## Fix

Pull request runs compare the merge commit with its first parent (`--against HEAD^1`, `fetch-depth: 2`) and judge only the PR's own change.
Pushes to `main` and manual runs keep the absolute baseline gate.

An increase fails a PR only for a `Deno.*` API listed in `kRalDenoReplacements`: an exact key whose `src/deno_ral` replacement is equivalent today (`build.os` and `build.arch`, in the scopes that can import `deno_ral`; not in `resources`, `src-js` or `src/core/lib`, which the browser-side YAML intelligence imports).
Every other increase is a warning on the added line plus a job summary with the per-scope delta and a maintainer step: update the branch with `main`, run `--update-baseline --accept-increase`, push the baseline change to the PR.
The summary prints the expected counts after merge.

Increases net out per Deno API and per std module before any file is blamed, so a renamed file or a moved call is not a finding.
std imports are never errors: whether a `deno_ral` wrapper replaces an import depends on the symbols used, on submodule semantics (`path/posix`) and on type exports, which a name check cannot establish.
They get a suggested module from `kStdSuggestions` in the warning.

`--accept-increase` replaces `--accept-tests-increase` and accepts any scope, since an uncovered increase in `src` needs a bump as well.
A PR that adds a `deno_ral` replacement adds its keys to `kRalDenoReplacements` in the same change (rule added to `_TEMPLATE.md`), which turns later increases of that API into errors.

PR comments were not used: fork PRs have a read-only token, and `pull_request_target` is not worth its security surface for text the job summary already carries.

Replaying the two incidents on Windows 11:

- #15134 on the ratchet commit: five warnings (`+6` in `tests`), the maintainer block with `tests 832 / 177`, exit 0.
- #15136 on the red `main`: the notice `main is above tools/runtime-boundary-baseline.json (tests Deno.* calls 832 > 826); not caused by this PR`, no warning, exit 0.
- A new `Deno.build.os` in `src`: the error with the added line number, exit 1.

title: Fix pdf-standard with KOMA classes under KOMA-Script 3.49.3
description:
KOMA-Script 3.49.3 (on CTAN since 2026-10-19) stops with `\DocumentMetadata not supported!` in all KOMA classes when `\DocumentMetadata` is used. Quarto emits `\DocumentMetadata` when `pdf-standard` is set, and our default PDF class is `scrartcl`, so any `pdf-standard` render to PDF fails as soon as TeX Live is updated. This is what turned our nightly smoke tests red; details in #15143.

## Fix

KOMA defines its check `\komascript_documentmetadata_test:` only if the macro does not already exist. Its source documents this as the way for packages and wrapper classes to replace the test before loading the class. When `pdf-standard` is set, `template.tex` now defines it as a no-op right after `\DocumentMetadata`. This gives back the 3.49.2 behaviour: same class, same layout, same output as with Quarto 1.9 and 1.10. Non-KOMA classes never read this macro.

`document-metadata.latex` is not modified, so it stays identical to Pandoc's partial.

This bypasses a check KOMA added on purpose. KOMA classes still don't tag sectioning commands (#14422), so the tagged PDF has the same structure issues as before this KOMA release. Proper tagging with `pdf-standard` will be handled separately for 1.11. KOMA describes the hook as provisional, so a later KOMA release may need another approach.

A backport to v1.10 will follow in a separate PR once this is merged.

## Test plan

Rendered locally all LaTeX docs in `tests/docs/smoke-all/pdf-standard/`, `tests/docs/render/pdf-standard-env.qmd`, a book project (`scrreprt`) with `pdf-standard: ua-2`, and a doc with `documentclass: article`, using KOMA-Script 3.49.2 and 3.49.3 (through `TEXMFHOME`).

- [x] Without the fix, every doc emitting `\DocumentMetadata` fails with 3.49.3 and renders with 3.49.2
- [x] With the fix, every doc renders with both versions, with the same results as 3.49.2 without the fix
- [x] With 3.49.2, the generated `.tex` only differs by the new block, and does not change at all without `pdf-standard`

Fixes #15143

title: Add mermaid-scale option to resize Mermaid images
description:
## Description

Adds a `mermaid-scale` option that resizes Mermaid diagrams rendered as images by a percentage of their natural size. Proposed in #15069.

With `mermaid-format: png` or `svg`, Quarto sizes each diagram at its natural size at 96 dpi, so Mermaid's 16px text prints at 12pt and wide diagrams can run past the page in Typst and PDF output. `fig-width` scales each diagram by a different factor, so every diagram ends up with a different text size. `mermaid-scale` applies one factor to every diagram's natural size, which keeps diagram text the same size across a document.

````md
---
format:
  typst:
    mermaid-format: png
    mermaid-scale: 75%
---

```{mermaid}
%%| mermaid-scale: 50%
flowchart LR
  A --> B
```
````

- The value is a percentage and keeps the aspect ratio. A cell value overrides the document value.
- An explicit `fig-width` or `fig-height` still takes precedence, so explicit sizes are respected as discussed in #8543.
- It applies to the `png` and `svg` outputs, where Quarto computes the size in `resolveSize`. With `mermaid-format: js`, mermaid.js sizes the diagram in the browser, so the option has no effect.
- The cell schema in the Mermaid handler and `document-mermaid.yml` both validate the value. A bare number or another string fails with a validation error instead of a `TypeError`.
- The option is skipped when the cell's options are written to the output div, like `mermaid-format`.

The editor tooling files under `src/resources/editor/tools/` were regenerated with `quarto dev-call build-artifacts`.

### Tests

`tests/smoke/render/render-mermaid-scale.test.ts` renders three copies of a diagram to Typst: one at `mermaid-scale: 100%`, one inheriting the document's `50%`, and one with `fig-width: 3`. It checks that the scaled image is half the size of the 100% one and that `fig-width` wins. It compares against the 100% copy instead of absolute sizes, so it does not depend on the fonts headless Chrome uses. With the scaling disabled the test fails (2.13in against an expected 1.065in).

The existing Mermaid smoke-all documents (`mermaid-typst`, `mermaid-multi-diagram`, `mermaid-pdf-default`, `mermaid-svg-docx`, `13661`, `mermaid-gfm-svg`, `mermaid-gfm-default`, `mermaid/backticks`, `mermaid-themes/3328`) still pass.

title: Update Deno to 2.9.8 for the eMudhra certificate distrust
description:
The bundled Deno 2.7.14 still trusts the eight eMudhra / emSign intermediates whose private keys are recoverable, so every HTTPS request Quarto makes from Deno (`quarto publish`, `quarto add`, `quarto use template`, `quarto install`) accepts certificates minted with them. Deno 2.9.8 is the first release that distrusts them (denoland/deno#37046), so the version bump is the fix. A 2.9.x below 2.9.8 is not enough, and `DENO_TLS_CA_STORE` can't work around it since our launchers always set it to `system,mozilla`.

With the dev build on 2.9.8, the probe from #15152 now rejects both eMudhra test endpoints with `invalid peer certificate: CertDistrusted`, with `DENO_TLS_CA_STORE` unset and with the launcher value, while github.com still fetches fine. Deno 2.7.14 accepts both.

## Changes required by Deno 2.9

- Vendor scripts use `--allow-import` instead of `--allow-all`. Deno 2.9 rejects permission flags on a non-global `deno install` (denoland/deno#36489), and because `vendor.sh` / `vendor.cmd` continue on error, configure finished normally but left the Deno cache empty.
- TypeScript 6 type errors that failed `deno test`: JSON imports move from `assert` to `with` (TS2880), the Posit Connect Cloud client takes `Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>` for fetch bodies, and test timer handles use `ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>`. All three also type-check on 2.7.14. The editor tooling bundles are regenerated after the `with` change; esbuild now wraps the JSON module as ESM, same data and same `.default`.
- `findOpenPort` excluded 4160 as "sieve", but the Fetch standard's bad port is 4190. Browsers always refused 4190, and Deno 2.9 now applies the same list to its own `fetch`, so a server started there could not even be polled for readiness (headless Chrome falls back to `findOpenPort` when 9222 is busy). The new test asks Deno's `fetch` which ports it blocks, so it follows the runtime list.
- `logError` prints the `cause` chain. Deno 2.9 reports every failed fetch as `TypeError: fetch failed` with the reason in `cause`, so `quarto add` against a server with an expired certificate said only "fetch failed" where 2.7 said "invalid peer certificate: certificate expired". No Quarto code creates errors with a cause, so only runtime errors gain the extra text.

The cross-version Deno KV cache problem (caches written by 2.9.8 breaking older Quarto) is already handled by #15180, which this PR builds on.

The website test fixtures also get the `**/*.quarto_ipynb` `.gitignore` entry that rendering appends, so a local smoke test run leaves the tree clean.

Fixes #15157

Refs #15152

title: Fix renders failing with RangeError when a Quarto cache is damaged
description:
When a Quarto cache file is damaged, `quarto check` and every render fail with `ERROR: RangeError: could not deserialize value`, with no hint at which file is at fault. In #15119 the user Sass cache (`~/.cache/quarto/sass`) got damaged after restoring a home folder from an external drive, and deleting that folder by hand was the only way out.

## Root cause

Both caches keep their index in Deno KV: the Sass cache in `src/core/sass/cache.ts` and the project cache in `src/core/cache/cache.ts`. A `kv.get()` on a row whose value can't be deserialized throws, and nothing caught it, so the error ended the render. Reproduced with 1.10.19 by zeroing the value of the Sass cache `version` row with `sqlite3`.

## Fix

A new `src/deno_ral/kv.ts` wraps every KV call of both caches and sorts errors by message, as Deno gives them no code:

1. A damaged value (`could not deserialize value`, an unknown value encoding, an invalid column type) is read as a cache miss. Quarto warns once per cache file, and the write that follows the miss repairs the row. This is the #15119 case.
2. A damaged file (`database disk image is malformed`, `file is not a database`) fails with a single error line naming the file and the folder to delete.
3. Any other error (locked store, unopenable path, closed handle) is rethrown with the cache path added, and never treated as damage.

Quarto never deletes a cache file itself. Deleting a store that another Quarto process has open is unsafe with SQLite, and the forms of damage found while testing are open-ended, so deleting the folder is left to the user with the error saying which one.

The new tests build really damaged stores (values zeroed with `node:sqlite`, truncated files, a text file in place of the database) instead of mocking errors.
