title: Update FluentUI in quarto-preview webui and rebuild bundle
description:
Combines the Snyk upgrades in #15181 and #15182 into one PR.

Both edit the same `package.json` and lockfile, so they conflict when landed one after the other. Snyk also never rebuilds the committed `src/webui/quarto-preview/dist/quarto-preview.js`, so each PR fails `runtime-boundary` on a dirty tree after configure rebuilds the webui. That red CI says nothing about the bump itself, but it blocks both PRs.

## Dependencies

- `@fluentui/react-components` goes from `~9.48.0` to `~9.74.9`. The tilde pin on the minor is kept, where #15181 loosened it to `^9.74.9`.
- `@fluentui/react-icons` goes from `^2.0.302` to `^2.0.343`, inside the existing range.

The 9.48 to 9.74.9 changelogs declare no breaking changes for the components, tokens and themes used by the preview UI. The places most likely to shift were the `Popover` positioning in `meca.tsx`, the `Dialog` custom `maxHeight` and motion changes in `ProgressDialog.tsx`, and the `ProgressBar` refactor.

## Test plan

Checked with the locally built `quarto preview` on a small website:

- [x] progress dialog while rendering (Cancel button), and error dialog with the dismiss icon, which closes on click
- [x] MECA "Preview Not Available" popover opens below the link, centered on it
- [x] light and dark themes apply to the popover
- [x] no browser console errors

title: Report runtime boundary increases a PR has already accepted as notices
description:
Follow-up to #15153.
In pull request mode the runtime boundary check compares the merge commit with the base branch only, so it never sees the PR's own `tools/runtime-boundary-baseline.json`.
#15180 ran the maintainer step (`--update-baseline --accept-increase`, `tests` 832 → 838) and the check still reported the six new calls as warnings saying "a maintainer accepts the new count before merging", with the "Maintainer action before merging" block in the job summary ([run](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/actions/runs/39941550538)).
A reviewer cannot tell from the check whether the step is done.

## Fix

PR mode now also reads the baseline in the merge commit.
When the PR raised a count there and the merge result does not exceed it, each finding for that count is a notice ("accepted by this PR's `tools/runtime-boundary-baseline.json`") on the added line, and the summary lists it under "Accepted in this PR" with the old and new baseline value.
This is the comparison the push check on `main` makes after merge.

A count is accepted only when the PR raised it.
Room left in `main`'s baseline (a count below its baseline because nobody lowered it) does not hide a new call: it stays a warning.
A baseline raised before updating the branch with `main`, and now too low for the merge result, also keeps the warnings and the maintainer block.
Errors for a `Deno.*` API that `src/deno_ral` replaces do not depend on the baseline and are unchanged.

The new test runs the script with `quarto run --dev ... --against HEAD` in a temporary git repo, like CI does: before the fix it showed the same warning and maintainer block as #15180.

title: Keep Deno KV caches per V8 release branch
description:
Deno 2.9 writes V8 serializer format 16 where 2.7 writes 15, and an older V8 rejects newer formats. Once a Quarto on Deno 2.9 touches the shared `sass.kv` or a project's `.quarto/project-cache/deno-kv-file`, every older Quarto on the machine fails to render with `RangeError: could not deserialize value` until the cache is deleted. The reverse direction is fine, 2.9 reads 2.7 data. This has to land before the Deno bump in #15157 (#15152), and in any 1.10.x backport of it.

Released Quarto cannot be fixed on its read side, so the new Quarto must never write a store that older versions open. Both caches now live in a `v8-<major>.<minor>` subdirectory, taken from `Deno.version.v8`, holding the KV file and its data files. A separate index in the same directory would let two versions overwrite each other's `<hash>.css` or content files. Untagged stores are left untouched, so older versions keep using them.

Alternatives considered: treating a deserialize error as a cache miss only helps versions that already contain the change, and tagging by Deno version instead of V8 branch would invalidate the cache on every patch bump. Old tagged directories are not pruned. This is an interim measure until the cache moves off Deno KV in the runtime migration.

## Project cache `clear()`

`clear()` passed each index entry's value to `join()` as if it were a hash, but disk entries store `{hash, type}` and immediate entries store `{value, type}`, so any populated cache threw `Path must be a string`. Its only caller is `init()` when the stored cache version is unknown, which is exactly the cache written by a newer Quarto, so it is reachable from this change's scenario. It now removes the hash file only for disk entries, with `safeRemoveSync` since entries with identical content share one file.

title: Fix listing styles overriding theme defaults in websites
description:
## Description

Fixes #15176.

`quarto-listing.scss` opened its variables with `/*-- scss:variables --*/`, which is not a layer boundary, so they stayed in the functions layer and were set before the theme's `!default` values. I changed it to `/*-- scss:defaults --*/`.

title: Fix citation BibTeX copy button shown with `code-copy: false`
description:
With `code-copy: false`, the BibTeX block in the citation appendix still gets a copy button that does nothing. Found while reviewing #14387, which moved the button inside the BibTeX block and made it more visible.

## Root cause

`processDocumentAppendix` adds the `code-with-copy` class, the `code-copy-outer-scaffold` wrapper and the copy button to the BibTeX block unconditionally, and has done so since the block was made copyable in 2022. With `code-copy: false`, clipboard.js and the ClipboardJS setup script are not added to the page, so nothing is wired to the button.

## Fix

The appendix now only adds the class, scaffold and button when code copy is enabled, using the same resolution as the other code blocks of the document. With `code-copy: false` the BibTeX block is still rendered, without the button.

That resolution was inlined twice in `format-html.ts`. It moves to `formatHasCodeCopy()` in `format-html-shared.ts`, together with `htmlFormatFeatureDefaults()` so the `minimal` default stays computed in one place. The shared module was chosen because the appendix cannot import `format-html.ts` without a cycle (`format-html.ts` imports the bootstrap postprocessor, which calls the appendix).

Fixes #15207

title: Fix BibTeX citation decoding HTML entities in the HTML appendix
description:
When a document title contains text that looks like an HTML entity, the BibTeX citation in the HTML appendix does not show the BibTeX Pandoc produced. `R\&notebook` displays as `R\¬ebook`, `a\<b` as `a\<b`, and the copy button copies this altered text.

## Root cause

The BibTeX is the plain text output of `pandoc -t biblatex`, but `createCodeBlock` inserted it with `innerHTML`, so the HTML parser decoded any `&` sequence forming an entity, including legacy ones without semicolon like `&not`. `innerHTML` comes from the original appendix block and the BibTeX string never carried markup. A `<` in the title is not affected as Pandoc writes it `\textless`.

## Fix

`createCodeBlock` now sets the text content of the code block. The appendix BibTeX block is its only caller.

Setting text skips the HTML parser's newline normalization too, and Pandoc writes CRLF on Windows, so the text goes through `normalizeNewlines` to keep the LF line endings the block had. Rendering the 19 citation smoke-all documents with and without the change gives identical HTML, apart from the two titles with entity-like text.

`createCodeBlock` is also modified by #15209, which may need a small rebase depending on merge order.

Fixes #15210

title: Fix website listings stacking update handlers on hash change
description:
Website listings attached another `list.on("updated")` handler on every URL hash change, and a page with several listings started with extra ones, so a single listing update reran the same work several times. Found while reviewing #9469, details in #15206.

## Fix

`window["quarto-listing-loaded"]` now wires each listing once, keyed by its id, and the hash handling moved to its own `applyListingHash()`. The `hashchange` listener emitted for each listing in `website-listing-template.ts` is replaced by a single one in `quarto-listing.js` that only applies the hash. That listener came from 962d83dbe for #1139, and back/forward between categories still relies on it.

`applyListingHash()` returns early when no listing is registered yet, as the single listener is now attached before any listing script runs.

## Tests

`listing-interactions.spec.ts` pins the current category, page hash, back/forward, progressive image and no-matching behavior on a page with two paginated listings. It passes before and after the fix.

`listing-update-handlers.spec.ts` counts handler runs for one `list.update()`. Before the fix, the first listing ran it 2 times after load, and the two listings 8 and 7 times after three hash changes. It is now 1 in every case.

Fixes #15206

title: Fix empty item links in listings when a description contains a link
description:
When a listing item description contains a link, default and grid listings render empty, focusable `<a>` elements, flagged by axe-core (`link-name`), and part of the item no longer links to the item. This is a regression from 1.7, see #15211.

## Root cause

The `delink` filter turns links inside a Div with the `delink` class into spans, so the whole description stays one link to the item. It only matches Pandoc Divs. The changes for #11758 (f9a52508e, 43ff451ee) moved the `<div class="delink listing-description">` container of the default and grid item templates into raw HTML blocks. The filter stopped running, and the description link ended up nested in the item link, which the browser splits into empty links.

## Fix

The container is a fenced div again, `::: {.delink .listing-description}` in the default template and `::: {.card-text .listing-description .delink}` in the grid template, with only the item link kept as raw HTML, like the `::: {.body}` div the template already uses. Markdown in descriptions keeps working, and the output is the same as in 1.6.

Links in descriptions not being clickable is the intended behavior, see #10814 where making them clickable is discussed as an option. So the links are turned into text again rather than kept.

## Tests

A smoke-all project checks, for default and grid listings, that the description has no link, keeps the link text, and stays inside the item link.

Some tests from #9469 relied on the description link:

- the listing axe test excluded the empty links, this exclusion is removed;
- the test checking the external icon of the description link is removed, as there is no description link anymore;
- the custom icon pagination test now uses a table listing, whose title link is the item link that keeps the external icon.

Fixes #15211

title: Fail the runtime boundary PR check on counts main would reject
description:
Follow-up to #15153 and #15183.
#15202 added four `Deno.*` calls in `tests/unit/zip.test.ts`. Its Runtime Boundary run was green, with warnings saying "a maintainer accepts the new count before merging" ([run](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/actions/runs/40488895545)). It merged without the baseline update, and the push check on `main` failed from 55a313cce ([run](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/actions/runs/40495916605)) until 4bebcb499 raised `tests` 870 → 874.
In pull request mode only a `Deno.*` API that `src/deno_ral` replaces is an error. Every other increase is a warning and the job exits 0, so the maintainer step depends on someone reading the summary of a green check.

## Fix

A PR run now fails when a count is above the PR's own `tools/runtime-boundary-baseline.json`, the comparison the push check on `main` makes after merge.
A green PR no longer turns `main` red.

The remedy is unchanged and stays with the maintainer: update the branch with `main`, run `--update-baseline --accept-increase`, push the baseline to the PR.
Per-line findings stay warnings, as the code is fine as written. They, one `::error` and the job summary tell the contributor there is nothing to change in the PR and that the check stays red until a maintainer accepts the count.

A count the PR did not raise but that fits under its baseline (`main` below its baseline because nobody lowered it) is now a notice and does not fail, as `main` will not fail on it either.
#15183 kept it a warning. With a failing check that would leave a PR red that `--accept-increase` cannot fix, since it writes a value at or under the old baseline.

A label to clear the check was considered and rejected: the merged tree would still carry the old baseline, and `main` would fail the same way.

Replaying #15202 (55a313cce against its parent) with this branch exits 1 with the four `zip.test.ts` warnings. With the baseline from 4bebcb499 applied it exits 0 and lists `tests` 870 → 874 under "Accepted in this PR".
The PR-mode test from #15183 now checks the exit status: its unaccepted case exited 0 before the fix.

`dev-docs/runtime-migration/README.md` records the decision for the PR 02c plan, and `_TEMPLATE.md` tells plans that raise a count to run `--accept-increase` in their own PR.

title: Fix contents shortcode decoding of non-internal raw inlines
description:
The contents shortcode filter produces unexpected character '<' errors and malformed-document warnings on ordinary input, and might remove it from the output. This is because it attempts to JSON-decode any paragraph or plain block containing a single raw inline, without checking its format.

For instance, in the smoke-test example the filter spams console output with the following ERROR/WARNING messages:

```
ERROR (/opt/quarto/share/pandoc/datadir/_json.lua:212) unexpected character '<' at line 1 col 1
WARNING (/opt/quarto/share/filters/main.lua:16354) [Malformed document] Failed to decode quarto-internal JSON: 
/opt/quarto/share/pandoc/datadir/_json.lua:193: bad 'for' initial value (number expected, got nil)
. Removing from document.
ERROR (/opt/quarto/share/pandoc/datadir/_json.lua:212) unexpected character '<' at line 1 col 1
WARNING (/opt/quarto/share/filters/main.lua:16354) [Malformed document] Failed to decode quarto-internal JSON: 
/opt/quarto/share/pandoc/datadir/_json.lua:193: bad 'for' initial value (number expected, got nil)
. Removing from document.
```

The proposed fix is to only decode raw inlines with format quarto-internal, matching the checks elsewhere in the filter.

Also, a small smoke test is added, which verifies that raw HTML survives in paragraphs and list items, that content reuse still works, and that rendering emits no errors or warnings.

title: ci: fall back off a slow Azure apt mirror in smoke tests
description:
On ubuntu runners, apt installs in the smoke tests sometimes crawl on a degraded `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` node. In [this job](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/actions/runs/39976686690/job/120493217209) from #15186, `Set up R` took 20 minutes and `Install Playwright system dependencies` failed at its 15 minute limit.

## Root cause

The degraded node serves package indexes at full speed but archives at tens of kB/s. The runner images set `Acquire::Retries 1` and `Acquire::http::Timeout 15`, which only catch a total stall, so apt never moves to `archive.ubuntu.com`, the next entry in `/etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt`. This is actions/runner-images#14823, still open (a fix is proposed in actions/runner-images#14596).

## Fix

The Azure line is dropped from `apt-mirrors.txt` only when the mirror is measured slow, so healthy runs keep using it and the load does not move to Canonical's servers.

- Before `setup-r`, whose apt calls can't be wrapped, a new step downloads one multi-megabyte `.deb` from the Azure mirror with `curl --speed-limit`, and drops the mirror if the speed stays under 1 MB/s for 10 seconds.
- The same step writes a small helper, `$APT_WITH_FALLBACK`, used by the Playwright deps step and the two `apt-get` steps. Each attempt gets 3 minutes (healthy runs take 20 to 45 seconds). After a failed attempt, the mirror is dropped, `dpkg --configure -a` finishes an install the timeout interrupted, and the command is retried.

Both checks are needed: the speed sample is one point in time, and a node can start fast and slow down in the middle of a download.

The logic is inline in `test-smokes.yml` rather than a local composite action, because release mode in `test-smokes-built.yml` checks out older tags that would not contain the action directory.

## Testing

Tested with throwaway probe workflows on a fork, running the step text from `test-smokes.yml`:

- The degraded node showed up live in some runs. Attempts were killed at 3 minutes and the retry finished in about 50 seconds on `archive.ubuntu.com`.
- With traffic from the Azure mirror throttled to 50 kB/s, the speed check dropped it and `setup-r` downloaded everything from `archive.ubuntu.com`.
- Healthy runs kept using the Azure mirror.

The `dpkg --configure -a` recovery was not exercised, as the probes only killed attempts during the download.

title: Fix zip extraction on Windows when Group Policy blocks temporary .bat files
description:
On Windows machines where a Group Policy blocks running `.bat` files from the temporary folder, every zip extraction fails: `quarto add`, `quarto use template` and `quarto use brand` from GitHub (always downloaded as `.zip` on Windows), and `quarto install tinytex`. The debug log shows `cmd /c ...\quarto-safe-exec*.bat` then `ERROR: Failed to unzip template.` with the Group Policy block message.

This is the same environment as #14367, but a different call site. The fix for #14367 (#14273) moved dart-sass off the temporary `.bat`; `unzip()` in `src/core/zip.ts` still went through `safeWindowsExec`, which writes `quarto-safe-exec*.bat` into `%TEMP%` and runs it with `cmd /c`. That code is unchanged since 2022, so no released version works on such machines.

## Fix

`safeWindowsExec` exists for batch files, whose arguments only `cmd.exe` can parse. `powershell.exe` and the self-extracting TinyTeX `.exe` are real executables, so the `.bat` brought nothing here. Both are now launched directly, and arguments go through as UTF-16, so accented and CJK paths still work without `chcp 65001`.

The archive and destination paths are embedded in the PowerShell script as single-quoted literals, with every single-quote character doubled, including the curly forms PowerShell also accepts. Before, a path with an apostrophe (`O'Brien`, `D’Arcy`) broke the script. The new unit test captures that case, as the Group Policy itself can't be reproduced in a test.

The script sets `[Console]::OutputEncoding` to UTF-8, which replaces the output side of the removed `chcp 65001`. Without it, PowerShell's error message shows a non-ASCII path as `?` on a console using a code page such as 850.

Windows `tar.exe` (bsdtar) was considered instead of PowerShell and rejected: it fails to open an archive whose path is outside the ANSI code page, and skips zip entries with UTF-8 non-ASCII names.

Other `safeWindowsExec` callers (`tlmgr`, `fmtutil`, `reg.exe` lookups, `openUrl`) still use the temporary `.bat` and are not changed here.
